requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 sit on separate private networks and communicate through node1
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 (10.10.12.0/24, to node2) and eth2 (10.10.13.0/24, to node3) were addressed; node2/node3 ens7 addressed and routed via node1 as gateway. Connectivity verified end-to-end with ping over the private path in the final clean ansible-playbook run (cmd-048f20f131de41c6), and the manual test config that had been used to debug the VyOS session bug was explicitly reverted before the ansible-driven configuration became the authoritative source (cmd-f2646141a6784b52, cmd-785fa731777a4e2e).

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node2 toward node3 limited to 1 Mbit/s
requirements.summary: VyOS qos rate-control policy applying a tbf qdisc (rate 1Mbit burst 15Kb) was bound to node1 eth2 egress (the node3-facing interface). Direct evidence: `tc qdisc show dev eth2` returns the tbf shaper, and an iperf3 throughput test from node2 to node3 measured ~0.99 Mbit/s, matching the intended limit.

requirements.requirement: Traffic from node3 toward node2 left unrestricted
requirements.summary: node1 eth1 (node2-facing) retained the default fq_codel qdisc with no rate-control policy attached. An iperf3 test from node3 to node2 measured ~1.05 Gbit/s, confirming the reverse direction is not throttled.

requirements.requirement: Implementation delivered via Ansible rather than manual one-off commands
requirements.summary: A playbook (/root/playbook.yml) and inventory (/root/inventory.ini) on the node4 control node drive the VyOS config (via vyos ssh + sudo bash wrapping configure/commit/save) and the node2/node3 addressing/routing (via ansible.builtin.raw, required due to ansible-core 2.20 being incompatible with Ubuntu 16.04's Python 2.7/3.5). The final successful end-to-end run (cmd-048f20f131de41c6) applies all configuration through the playbook and is idempotent (re-run after node4's reboot succeeded cleanly).

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 baseline/disruption/recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 2eb8b6e8 captured pre-reboot; node became unreachable across several polls during the restart window; post-reboot boot_id 90af458c (changed) observed; recovery confirmed via restored eth1/eth2 addressing, the 1Mbit tbf qdisc on eth2, ip_forward=1, and persisted qos config in config.boot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node2 baseline/disruption/recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 6ab98831 captured; connection refused during restart window; post-reboot boot_id 6ffa2b2d (changed); recovery confirmed via ens7 address, route to 10.10.13.0/24, and successful ping to node3.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 baseline/disruption/recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id b185f188 captured; connection refused during restart window; post-reboot boot_id ab4525b3 (changed); recovery confirmed via ens7 address, route to 10.10.12.0/24, and successful ping to node2.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node4 baseline/disruption/recovery
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 6fd57414 captured; unreachable during restart window; post-reboot boot_id 4c813570 (changed); recovery confirmed via intact ansible tooling/files, discovery and correction of a persistence gap (vyos SSH key needed to be added via the VyOS config tree rather than raw authorized_keys to survive node1's own reboot), and a fully successful post-reboot idempotent playbook re-run across all three managed nodes.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, corroborating evidence: node1 mediates the node2/node3 private-network topology, node1's VyOS QoS policy applies a 1Mbit tbf shaper specifically to the node3-facing egress interface while the node2-facing interface is left with the default unrestricted qdisc, and iperf3 measurements from both directions (0.99 Mbit/s node2->node3 vs 1.05 Gbit/s node3->node2) directly confirm the asymmetric limit is enforced at runtime. The entire configuration is driven by a final, idempotent Ansible playbook run rather than the manual commands used earlier for troubleshooting the VyOS config-session bug, and those manual changes were deliberately reverted before the authoritative playbook run. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was executed on all four managed nodes with clear baseline/disruption/changed-boot-id/recovery evidence, including discovery and correction of an SSH-key persistence gap on the VyOS router.
limitations: A root SSH authorized_keys entry added to node1 during troubleshooting (cmd-58fa68e2007748c5) was never explicitly removed or confirmed absent in a later snapshot; its live login test failed, suggesting it is currently inert, but this could not be independently re-verified beyond that one failed SSH attempt.

Fixed lifecycle snapshots (before/after prepare, after executor) capture only coarse indicators (boot-id, listening sockets, temp files, package health) and do not include tc qdisc state or the private-network addressing, so the QoS and topology conclusions rely on the executor's own captured command output rather than the fixed collector snapshots.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing troubleshooting during the extended VyOS config-session debugging was bounded and either reverted or superseded by the final ansible-driven configuration: a manual tc qdisc test (cmd-3a57d853f4624ff3) was deleted immediately after confirming syntax; a manual eth1/eth2 address set as root (cmd-fe86cbe4f2864901) was explicitly reverted (cmd-f2646141a6784b52) before being reapplied through the playbook path (cmd-785fa731777a4e2e); several /tmp debug shell scripts (dbg*.sh, vyos-config*.sh) were low-risk and left in /tmp with no functional impact. One residual mutation was not cleaned up: a root SSH public key was appended to node1's /root/.ssh/authorized_keys (cmd-58fa68e2007748c5) while diagnosing a permission bug in the vyos config session; this key was never removed even though the executor's own connectivity test for it failed (cmd-67fc03586d6e4f46) and the final solution instead uses the vyos user's key added through VyOS's own config tree. This is a bounded, apparently-inert but unreverted expansion of SSH access surface on the router and should have been cleaned up.
